questions.q: What is the defining difference between asynchronous and synchronous communication?
options: Asynchronous communication can never involve two Salesforce orgs
In asynchronous communication, the caller continues its own work immediately instead of blocking to wait for a response
Asynchronous communication always uses more network bandwidth than synchronous communication
Asynchronous communication only works for batch jobs, never for individual records
questions.explain: The defining trait of asynchronous communication is that the caller doesn't block — it sends the request or publishes the event and moves on, removing the availability coupling that synchronous communication creates.

questions.q: A system publishes a Platform Event announcing that an Opportunity closed, with no need to know whether any particular subscriber processed it. Which asynchronous sub-pattern does this describe?
options: Synchronous request-reply
Fire-and-forget
Asynchronous request-reply
Point-to-point batch synchronization
questions.explain: Fire-and-forget is the sub-pattern where the publisher genuinely has no need to track or learn the outcome of what it triggered — exactly the case for a broadcast-style event with no correlation back to the publisher.

questions.q: What mechanism does asynchronous request-reply typically rely on so the caller can eventually learn the outcome of a request it didn't wait for?
options: A correlation identifier that tags the original request so a later result or callback can be matched back to it
A hard-coded wait of exactly 10 seconds before checking the result
The caller re-sends the exact same request every few seconds until it gets a response
Asynchronous request-reply never needs any tracking mechanism at all
questions.explain: Asynchronous request-reply uses a correlation ID: the caller tags its request with a unique identifier, continues its own work, and later matches an incoming reply or poll result back to that same ID.

questions.q: What is Change Data Capture (CDC) built on, and what does it publish?
options: It is built on the Bulk API and publishes full nightly snapshots of every record
It is built on the Platform Events infrastructure and publishes change events — creates, updates, deletes, and undeletes — for selected Salesforce objects
It is a synchronous feature that blocks the publishing transaction until every subscriber confirms receipt
It is unrelated to Platform Events and uses its own separate event bus
questions.explain: Change Data Capture is built on top of the same Platform Events infrastructure, specifically generating change events for record creates, updates, deletes, and undeletes on selected objects, per Salesforce's Change Data Capture developer documentation.

questions.q: What real cost does this lesson say asynchronous communication introduces in exchange for removing the caller's blocking wait?
options: Asynchronous communication has no real costs; it strictly improves on synchronous communication in every way
It relocates complexity: debugging becomes harder since failures surface later and elsewhere, and subscribers must handle events that may not arrive in the order they were published
Asynchronous patterns always cost more money to license than synchronous ones
Asynchronous communication eliminates the need for any error handling
questions.explain: Going asynchronous doesn't eliminate complexity — it moves it: tracking outcomes needs a correlation mechanism, failures can surface far from their cause in time and system, and out-of-order delivery has to be designed for rather than assumed away.
